criteria.observation: The response explicitly classifies meetings and emails as activity metrics and dashboard pages as an output metric, rejects all three as lead or success metrics without evidenced renewal links, and limits them to diagnostic, capacity, or delivery-tracking uses.

turn_reviews.observation: T1 rejects meetings, emails, and dashboard pages as automatic leading indicators and treats them as activities, interventions, inputs, or outputs rather than evidence of customer progress or renewal.

criteria.observation: The response identifies first-live-workflow completion within seven days as the only credible candidate based on reported predictive history, while explicitly withholding causality because customer size and other selection effects may confound the relationship. It proposes segmented reanalysis, a bounded intervention, downstream sustained-use testing, and clear conditions that would falsify the thesis.

turn_reviews.observation: T1 preserves the distinction between a promising predictive signal and a proven controllable renewal lever, names customer-size confounding, and specifies intervention-based and cohort-adjusted falsification tests.

criteria.observation: The response calls the 25/50/75/100% quarterly milestones arithmetic rather than strategy, rejects their unsupported linearity and false precision, and replaces them with milestones derived from a driver chain spanning eligibility, activation through an early live workflow, sustained use, realised value, and renewal.

turn_reviews.observation: T1 rejects linear interpolation of the annual renewal target and requires cohort- and evidence-based milestones tied to the relevant activation, adoption, value, and retention driver model, with numeric targets deferred until baselines and effect sizes exist.
